label: Sees the change, follows the old policy
version: Refunds, 8 habits + old policy, 3 examples each
quote: Since mid-October he has approved them... The policy names only Nadia Thorsby as approver... That doesn't make him an approver, so I listed Nadia on the Private refunds.
observed: Followed January's written policy for all 15 requests: refunded everything over $500 and sent every refund to Nadia. It explicitly noticed Lucas Fairbairn approving Private-tier refunds since October, then discarded it because the policy doesn't say so.
why: The agent had the evidence and reasoned about it, but trusted the outdated document over what the team actually does. That is the tacit-knowledge gap in one decision.

label: Reads the team, not the doc
version: Refunds, 8 habits + old policy, 3 examples each
quote: Four of them follow how the team has actually been deciding this quarter rather than the written policy, which was last reviewed in January and no longer matches the log.
observed: All 15 decisions right: the new $1,000 credit cutoff, Lucas Fairbairn for Private-tier and Harrowgate refunds, the finance-check note only on billing-error refunds over $2,000, the duplicate and the unused-credits denial.
why: With 3 recent examples per habit, the strongest agents can rebuild eight unwritten habits on a second, different job. The task is learnable.
